page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture, powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor. The hardware setup includes 16 physical CPU cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 32 virtual CPUs and 64 GB of system memory, which yields a memory ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. Cache architecture features 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set availability includes AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2. The server contains no local SSD storage or GPU hardware, and public IPv4 addresses are not bundled. Baseline network throughput is rated at 16 Gbps.

Synthetic benchmark results reflect consistent multi-core processing performance, indicated by a PassMark CPU score of 34,961.9 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 30,977.29. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 126.91 GB/sec. In language model testing, the instance registers 266.46 tokens per second during small-model text generation. Key tradeoffs include complete reliance on attached network storage and modest memory allocation per vCPU, restricting suitability for large in-memory databases. The hardware profile offers balanced cost efficiency for core-heavy execution without hardware acceleration overhead. Recommended workloads include software compilation, web serving, ETL pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. It features 16 physical cores, 32 vCPUs, and 64 GB of memory, yielding a 2 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware capabilities include 48 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 VNNI support for specialized vector operations. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on external network storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reveal balanced compute execution, including a PassMark CPU score of 34,961.9 and 266.46 tokens per second in small-model LLM text generation. The 2:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides efficient compute density for CPU-bound tasks, though it limits suitability for memory-intensive applications. Recommended workloads include software compilation, web serving, batch data processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.
